sources.title: Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis & John Jumper awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry
sources.quote_checked: Receiving the Nobel Prize is the honour of a lifetime. | AlphaFold has already been used by more than two million researchers to advance critical work, from enzyme design to drug discovery. | I hope we'll look back on AlphaFold as the first proof point of AI's incredible potential to accelerate scientific discovery. | Co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs

sources.title: Demis Hassabis: Future of AI, Simulating Reality, Physics and Video Games (#475)
sources.quote_checked: My estimate is sort of 50% chance by in the next five years, so by 2030 let's say. | It isn't kind of a jagged intelligence where some things, it's really good at | you'd want that consistency of intelligence across the board | that's our sweet spot and I think that's harder. It's harder to invent things than to fast follow. | there's no such thing as failure really. As long as you are picking experiments and hypotheses that meaningfully split the hypothesis space | picking the right question is the hardest part of science | I'm not sure it's even desirable because that's a kind of hard takeoff scenario | I don't have a P-Doom number. The reason I don't is because I think it would imply a level of precision that is not there | it's definitely non-zero and it's probably non-negligible | it's clear to me the only rational, sensible approach is to proceed with cautious optimism | With AlphaGo, we just use Monte Carlo Tree Search and that's what found move 37, the new never seen before strategy in Go

sources.title: Demis Hassabis Thinks We're in the Foothills of the Singularity
sources.quote_checked: Step one: Solve intelligence. Step two: Use it to solve everything else. | And people were quite confused. But we really meant it. | Ten years from now, I think we'll realize that we were standing in the foothills of the singularity now.

sources.title: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis gets UK knighthood for 'services to artificial intelligence'
sources.quote_checked: services to artificial intelligence | Born in London in 1976 | lead programmer at Bullfrog Productions | Graduated from the University of Cambridge in Computer Science and earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience from University College London | Co-founded DeepMind in 2010 with Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman | Received a CBE in 2017 | Google acquired DeepMind in 2014

sources.title: Demis Hassabis – Facts
sources.quote_checked: Born: 27 July 1976, London, United Kingdom | Prize motivation: "for protein structure prediction" | Prize share: 1/4 | In 2020, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper presented an AI model called AlphaFold2. With its help, they have been able to predict the structure of virtually all known proteins.

sources.title: Google's AlphaGo AI wins astounding 4-1 victory against Lee Sedol
sources.quote_checked: I'm kind of speechless | DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis said in a post-game press conference | AlphaGo, an AI developed by Google's DeepMind project, has successfully defeated legendary Go player Lee Sedol
